properties.description: outlined rectangle about 0.8 by 3.5 m against the inside of the east wall of the north-east room with three short step lines at its south end on Ballu's plan, so a stepped platform or bench, or the foot of a stair to an upper floor; Ballu's text doesn't mention a stair, and it's faint at best on the satellite imagery, so uncertain

properties.description: two step lines against the south side of the frigidarium's south wall on Ballu's plan, so two steps between the frigidarium and the pool in the south apse room, nothing to see on the satellite imagery, so uncertain

properties.plan_source: Amraoui 2020b: 238 n. 5, size from fig. 11.5 (p. 229); round-2 drawing (Sep 29, 2026), notional place in room 3
properties.description: stair to an upper floor in room 3, from Amraoui's note that the house had an upper floor, "as indicated by the remains of a staircase in room 3" (2020b: 238 n. 5), but she doesn't draw it or say where in the room it stood, so its size and place here are notional, a single flight about 1.1 m wide and 3.7 m long, the size of the stair room on her plan of *insula* 20 next door (2020b: 229, fig. 11.5), against the east wall with its foot at the opening in the south-east corner of the room; nothing on the satellite imagery reads as a stair and Ballu doesn't mention one in this house (BCTH 1912: 494), so uncertain

properties.plan_source: Amraoui 2020b: 234 and fig. 11.10; round-2 drawing (Oct 3, 2026), notional place in room 9
properties.description: stair or ladder to an upper floor in room 9, from Amraoui's text, which says an entrance to the upper storey was found in room 9 near one of the entries from the street and next to the door into room 8, a ladder or wooden staircase of which no traces remain (2020b: 234), and her axonometric view draws a flight here (2020b: 235, fig. 11.10); its size and place are notional, a single flight about a metre wide and three long against the wall of rooms 8 and 9, its foot just inside the door between the two rooms and clear of the street opening, and nothing on the imagery reads as a stair, so uncertain

properties.plan_source: Amraoui 2020a: 134, fig. 4.11; Amraoui 2020b: 235, fig. 11.10; round-2 drawing (Oct 3, 2026), set between the wall lines of the imagery
properties.description: stair in the north-west corner of room 12, just east of the wall of rooms 11 and 12 and hanging from the fullery's south wall, an outlined flight about three quarters of a metre wide and two and a quarter long with its treads drawn at the south end on Amraoui's plan, and a small stepped block in the same corner on her axonometric view, so the stair itself survived; she doesn't mention it in her text, and nothing of it shows on the ground, so probable on her plan's word

properties.plan_source: Ballu, Rapport 1923: 43 (plan), 45-46; Ballu, Rapport 1922: 47-53; Germain 1969: 81, fig. 10; round-2 drawing (Oct 3, 2026), set on the wall lines of the imagery
properties.description: the steps of the main entrance's porch on the street, drawn with their treads in front of the door on Ballu's plan, the porch paved in stone on two columns (1923: 46); on the ground the street edge here is unclear, so probable

properties.plan_source: Ballu, Rapport 1923: 43 (plan), 45-46; Ballu, Rapport 1922: 47-53; Germain 1969: 81, fig. 10; round-2 drawing (Oct 3, 2026), set on the wall lines of the imagery
properties.description: the five steps at the end of the corridor from the vestibule, at the atrium's south walk (Ballu 1923: 46), drawn as treads against the walk's back wall on his plan; the house's floors were 1.20 m below the shops' (1922: 47), so these probably went down into the house, probable

properties.plan_source: Ballu, Rapport 1923: 43 (plan), 45-46; Ballu, Rapport 1922: 47-53; Germain 1969: 81, fig. 10; round-2 drawing (Oct 3, 2026), set on the wall lines of the imagery
properties.description: the steps at the opening between the secondary entrance and the antechamber, drawn as treads on Ballu's plan, his antechamber with four steps of 0.30 m that made up the 1.20 m between the shops' floors and the house's (1922: 47), so probable

the staircase to the upper floor in the room Ballu calls the stair cage, reached by the opening of 1.30 m at the south-west corner of the corridor, north of the fifth shop's back room, of which one step was left (1922: 48); his plan draws no stair, so its size and place are notional, a flight about 1.1 by 2.4 m against the room's east wall away from the doors, and it's uncertain

properties.plan_source: Ballu 1911a (Sept années): 74, plan of the house, with his description 72-73 (first published in his report on the 1906 excavations, Ballu 1907: 261-262); round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026), set on the walls as the imagery shows them
properties.description: the stair to the upper storey, to the left as you come in, of which seven steps were left (1911a: 72); drawn where the plan has it, between its two hatched piers, which aren't drawn, and the big dark mark just north of it on the imagery is most likely the shadow thrown by the pier and the steps still standing, so probable
